message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"apukeinoksi","gloss":"as an auxiliary means / helping device (translative case)","category":"means/aid","note":"Compound apu-keino: 'help-device/expedient'. Not 'lääke' (medicine). The sentence is rendered 'se on keksitty apukeinoksi muistille ja viisaudelle'; memory and wisdom are in the allative, 'for memory and wisdom'."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"muistille","gloss":"for memory (allative)","note":"Dative-like beneficiary: the aid is 'for memory'. Elsewhere in the same sentence Theuth's 'mnemonikōterous' is rendered 'muistiltaan paremmiksi' (better in their memory)."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"viisaudelle","gloss":"for wisdom (allative)","note":"Standard word viisaus, 'wisdom'. It is the ordinary, positive word here."},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"apuneuvoa","gloss":"an aid-instrument / helping tool (partitive)","category":"means/aid","note":"A different compound from 274e: apukeino (aid-device) versus apuneuvo (aid-tool). Both share the root 'apu-' (help) but are not the same word. Partitive because the clause is negated ('Et siis ole keksinyt apuneuvoa muistille')."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"muistille","gloss":"for memory (allative)","note":"Same form as at 274e, so memory is kept identical in both places."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"mieleenpalauttamiselle","gloss":"for the calling-back-to-mind (allative of a verbal noun)","note":"A literal calque on 'recalling to mind' (mieleen = to mind, palauttaminen = bringing back). It matches the verb 'palauttavat asioita mieleensä' used earlier in the speech."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"rikkiviisauden","gloss":"of broken/ruined wisdom (accusative)","note":"The word 'rikkiviisaus' (rikki = broken, viisaus = wisdom) is a coinage or rare word meaning sham wisdom. It folds the Greek δόξαν σοφίας ('the seeming of wisdom') into one word and drops the doxa/alētheia contrast on 'seeming'. The antithesis survives only in 'et todellista viisautta' ('not real wisdom')."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"rikkiviisaiksi","gloss":"into broken-wise / sham-wise (translative plural)","note":"Same stem as 'rikkiviisauden' at 275a, so the 'sham wisdom' and 'sham-wise' pair stays linked as in the Greek doxa/doxosophoi. It is contrasted with 'viisaiksi' (wise)."},"argument":"Lehmuskoski gives pharmakon a neutral helping-device sense (apukeino, apuneuvo) and avoids any word for medicine or poison, so the drug/cure/poison ambivalence is lost entirely. The two occurrences are also not the same word: Theuth's apukeino becomes Thamus's apuneuvo, so Thamus does not literally turn Theuth's own word against him, although the shared 'apu-' root keeps the connection audible. The memory/reminding contrast stays clear, and rikkiviisaus/rikkiviisaat preserves the wisdom/sham-wisdom link that closes the passage."}
